clips.text: Mrs. Hop has a large wing apartment at Wardman Park Hotel and will reopen It on her arrival, do ing most of her entertaining for the Winter at that hotel, at the Carlton and at the Chevy Chase Club.

A large number of dinner parties were given last evening preceding the dinner dance at Wardman Park Hotel, when a special entertainment pro gram was given In celebration of the eighth anniversary of the opening of the hotel.

In their state ments at Wardman Park Hotel Mr. Fall mentioned to Doheny the diffi culty he was having in getting the loan and that when he left the Sen ate he was going into private life and devote all time to this property.
Assistant Attorney General Mr. John Marshall, who is spending two weeks in Florida, will join Mrs. Mar- i shall and tneir family at Wardman Park Hotel the latter part of the month.

Mr. James Wilson, director of operations of the United States Ship ping Board, and Mrs. Wilson have re opened their appartment at Wardman Park Hotel after a six-week trip to Europe, which Mr. Wilson made in the interests of the United States lines.

note: Clips are machine-read text (OCR) from scanned Evening Star pages on the Library of Congress's Chronicling America, lightly cleaned (line-break hyphens rejoined, stray symbols removed); misspellings are the scanner's. Newspapers this old are public domain. Each clip links to its page at loc.gov. Clips that mention race, covenants, deed restrictions or slurs are skipped automatically (keyword list: race, races, racial, colored, coloured, negro, negroes, white only, whites only, for whites, white people, white persons, white residents, caucasian, segregation, segregated, covenant, covenants, restricted, restriction, restrictions, plus a list of slurs), because they need an editor's context; legal notices and lists of private individuals are skipped too.
